Herrera, Aguho, Pateros, 1640 Dear Mr. Jasarino: This has reference to your letter dated February 6, 2021, requesting for this Department's legal opinion concerning the authority of the Lupong Tagapamayapa of a Barangay under Section 408 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160). Per your letter, you are requesting for an advice on whether two individuals, one living in Taguig City and another in Cabuyao, Laguna, but both working in the same barangay, be considered "residents" so that a Barangay Lupong Tagapamayapa may exercise authority to bring them together for an amicable settlement. At the outset, may we invite your attention to Section 408 of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "Section 408. Subject Matter for Amicable Settlement; Exception Thereto. - The lupon of each barangay shall have authority to bring together the parties actually residinq in the same city or municipality for amicable settlement of all disputes except: X xxx xxx x x x x" (emphasis supplied) However, we also invite your attention to Section 409 of the same Code, to wit: Section 409. Venue. — (a) Disputes between persons actually residing in the same barangay shall be brought for amicable settlement before the lupon of said barangay. (b) Those involving actual residents of different barangays within the same city or municipality shall be brought in the barangay where the respondent or any of the respondents actually resides, at the election of the complaint. (c) All disputes involving real property or any interest therein shall be brought in the barangay where the real property or the larger portion thereof is situated. (d) Those arisinq at the workplace where the contendinq parties are emp!gyeLor at_the institution where such parties are enrolled for study, shall be brouqht in the baranqav where such workplace or institution is located. Objections to venue shall be raised in the mediation proceedings before the punong barangay; otherwise, the same shall be deemed waived. Any legal question which may confront the punong barangay in resolving objections to venue herein referred to may be submitted to the Secretary of Justice, or his duly designated representative, whose ruling thereon shall be binding." (emphasis ours) Based on the aforequoted provision, disputes between persons arising at the workplace where the contending parties are employed shall be brought in the barangay where such workplace is located. However, per your letter, it is not clear whether the contending parties are employed in the same workplace or not. What was merely stated was that they are working in the same barangay. In this regard, it is our view that the dispute between the contending parties may be brought in the barangay where the workplace is located even if the contending parties are residing in Taguig City and Cabuyao, Laguna, provided, however, that the dispute arose from the same workplace where the contending parties are employed, otherwise, the Lupong Tagapamayapa will have no authority over such disputes and parties. Also, please take note that the dispute must be between employees only in order for the Lupong Tagapamayapa to have authority. The Lupong Tagapamayapa has no authority if such dispute or controversy arose from employer-employee relationship. Art. 226 of the Labor Code, as amended, provides that the Department of Labor and Employment has original and exclusive jurisdiction over conciliation and mediation disputes, grievances, or problems arising from or affecting labor-management relations in all workplaces. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. ery truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE MARTIN B. DINO ECRETARY: Undersecretary for Barangay Affairs OUSBA/MBDILLLS-LRALLD/lasm "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54
